extracted.intended_audience: inventors, design patent applicants, and patent practitioners preparing U.S. design patent drawings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing drawings (or acceptable photographs/computer-generated images) for U.S. design patent applications so the illustrated ornamental features correctly define the enforceable scope of the design patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings define enforceable scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The ornamental features illustrated in the drawings define the enforceable scope of a design patent in the same way that claims define the enforceable scope of a utility patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure drawings clearly and accurately depict the novel ornamental features you wish to claim because those drawings (not separate claim text) determine what is claimed and enforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be sufficiently clear and detailed to accurately represent the claimed design and must depict every design feature the applicant wishes to claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include shape, configuration, ornamental design, surface ornamentation, and surface textures as necessary. Omissions or unclear depiction may prevent proper claiming of features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black-and-white default; color permitted with petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings are traditionally black-and-white line drawings; color drawings may be submitted only if necessary to illustrate the claimed design properly and require USPTO approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting color requires a petition and additional fee. If color drawings are submitted, include specification language such as: "The patent or application file contains at least one drawing executed in color. Copies of this patent or patent application publication with color drawing(s) will be provided by the Office upon request and payment of the necessary fee."

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete set of views (head-on)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a complete set of views to fully disclose the design's appearance, typically including front, rear, top, bottom, right and left sides, and isometric or perspective views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required views must be shown head-on (not from an angle). If needed, include exploded, sectional, or enlarged views to show depth and shape of three-dimensional objects or features. Duplicate or mirror views may be omitted only if the specification explicitly makes this clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solid vs broken (dashed) lines usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Solid lines depict all parts of the design claimed by the applicant; broken or dashed lines illustrate portions of the design not claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use broken lines to show context or unclaimed surrounding environment (e.g., showing the rest of an article in broken lines when only an element is claimed). Note that some foreign jurisdictions do not allow broken lines, meaning dashed-line features in a U.S. application may need to be shown as solid lines in foreign counterparts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface shading and texture conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper surface shading and texture must be used to indicate the character and contour of the design's surfaces and to differentiate open vs solid areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use accepted USPTO shading techniques (e.g., straight lines to indicate flat surfaces; stippling to indicate curved/non-flat surfaces). Inadequate shading in the originally filed drawings can lead to a non-enabling rejection; adding shading after filing can be considered new matter and is therefore problematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and uniformity across drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawings in an application must be consistent and drawn to the same scale, maintaining uniformity in size, shading, and line thickness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inconsistent scales, line weights, or shading between views can create discrepancies in interpretation of what is claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible graphic forms and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs and computer-generated drawings are allowed if they meet USPTO clarity, detail, and reproducibility requirements; photographs may be used when they are the only practicable medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not combine photographs with black-and-white line drawings in the same design application. Photographs should not show environmental structure (i.e., extraneous background/context that is not part of the claimed design). Ensure high reproducibility and clarity for non-line art media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheet size and margin requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must adhere to specified sheet sizes and margins to ensure uniformity and proper reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use A4 or 8.5 x 11 inch sheets. Maintain at least 1 inch top margin, at least 1 inch left margin, at least 5/8 inch right margin, and at least 3/8 inch bottom margin on each sheet.
